items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In fact, some time later, Cannonball told me that Eddie Cleanhead Vinson and I were his first idols, the first guys he ever heard in person that he really went for

ctx.x: In this particular group we had made a few alterations. We had a very fine pianist named Baby Lockett; a very good pianist. Her husband was named Jack Lockett. And Jack Scott, the guitar player; he was still with us.

While I'm there, there used to be some kids coming around outside and hang around outside to listen to me play. And it was Cannonball Adderley, hah-hah, and Nat Adderley, and Buster Cooper, and the little trumpet player from St. Petersburg (they were all from St. Petersburg) used to come over there...a little trumpet player named Frank Royal. In fact, some time later, Cannonball told me that Eddie Cleanhead Vinson and I were his first idols, the first guys he ever heard in person that he really went for, you…

So I had some great times there in Tampa. And this is where I also heard the Billy Eckstine band, the fourth day it was together. That's when he had Sarah, and in the reed section they had Charlie Parker playing the lead, and a little kid named Junior out of Kansas City playing the other also [JOHN JACKSON], Lucky Thompson was playing tenor, Leo Parker was playing the baritone, Art Blakey was on drums, Tommy Potter played the bass, and John Malachi on the piano. And in the trumpet section they had Gail Brockman…
